notes: Spawn x, y, z is the lizard body where it touches its perch, in the game frame. host.t names the list in placements.json (landmarks, plants, clumps rows), the logs list here, or the ground (i = -1); host.c, where given, indexes colliders.json circles: the stem the lizard clings to, or the stem its stub branch grows from. hag is the height above the host's base (the host's own y, the ground or water surface it stands on). Lizards at ground level (host ground, or on the ground at the foot of a host) have hag 0 and y on the terrain, which can differ from the host's y by a few centimetres; they always stand on walkable ground outside every collider. ang follows the terrain start heading: direction (-sin ang, 0, -cos ang), 0 = north (-z), positive towards west (-x), as three.js rotation.y. pose 'bark': clinging to a stem, belly towards the stem axis, head up, back facing along ang (ang points from the axis to the lizard); pose 'flat': lying on a roughly level surface (ground, log, branch, leaf, frond), head towards ang. Clinging lizards sit on a stem of radius dbh / 2 without taper. A flat lizard with host.c set lies on a short stub branch 0.2 m out from that stem's bark, below the host's crown: draw the stub from the stem out to the lizard. Leaf lizards sit just inside the host's foliage surface, modelled as an ellipsoid over the crown zone (landmarks: crown_base to height over crown_w_ew by crown_w_ns about crown_x, crown_z; plants and clumps: a disc of their width), or a dome from the ground for bushes, ground shrubs, shrubs and herbs. Branch lizards within the crown sit on a branch running out from the host axis along ang; in a host with no stem (bush, shrub, canopy puff) they sit in the outer part of the foliage. Understorey and mangrove clumps are taken to stand on one short stem at their x, z. perch is the perch class the lizard was recorded on; where no host of the matching kind was near, free, in the loop pole's reach and clear of the records (no lizard sits within 0.2 m of any record), the lizard sits on the nearest host that fits its recorded height, so a trunk lizard may lie flat on a low branch or in a bush: pose and host say how to draw it. Sampling: each species is stratified by perch in proportion to its records, going round the marked individuals inside each perch; the rare species (bark and knight anoles) use every record, a record out of reach being pulled in towards the nearest walkable ground and one perched above 3.5 m brought down to that height. Every lizard is within 2.0 m (plan) of ground the player can stand on and at most 4.0 m above it, its height is within 0.75 m of the record's, a host carries at most 6 lizards, and no lizard has more than its species' cap of same-species neighbours within 3 m (stats.caps). species.spawns counts this table. Logs: x, y, z is the ground under the middle of the log; the log is horizontal with its axis at y + r, along (cos rot, 0, -sin rot), that is a cylinder built along +x and turned by rotation.y = rot; logs lie on nearly level walkable ground (within 0.08 m along their length). Perch names: trunk, branch, ground, palm_stem, root, leaf, palm_frond, log. Sex: m, f, or u where the record has none. Rarity follows each species' share of the observations.
